benefits: Get a full device health summary in one page, no apps to install.
Spot the weak point fast: low battery, no cookies, slow network, small screen.
Share the report with support teams instead of describing your device.
Covers phones, tablets, laptops, and desktops with one honest checklist.

faqs.a: Auto-detect reads your user agent and screen to guess the device. It is usually right for phones and desktops, but tablets and 2-in-1 laptops can fool it. Pick your device from the list for a labelled report.
faqs.q: How accurate is the auto-detect device guess?

faqs.a: That is an info row, not a failure. Some values are hidden by browsers for privacy: Safari and Firefox rarely share memory size or battery level, and battery data is mostly a Chrome/Android feature.
faqs.q: Why do some rows say Info or Unknown?

faqs.a: Warnings flag things that might bite you: battery under 20 percent, fewer than 4 CPU cores, cookies disabled, or being offline. They are prompts to check, not proof of a defect.

No. The page reads values like screen size, CPU cores, and battery level through standard browser APIs and shows them on your screen. Copying the report is a manual action - nothing is transmitted automatically.
faqs.q: Is my device information sent anywhere?

faqs.a: The battery API is a Chrome and Edge feature, mostly on Android and laptops. If your browser does not support it, the row simply shows Unknown - everything else still works.
faqs.q: Why is the battery row unknown on my device?

faqs.a: Because not every phone exposes a useful gyroscope, magnetometer, or vibration motor to the browser. Those checks live on their own test pages (Gyroscope Test, Vibration Test) where the hardware is handled properly.
faqs.q: Why is there no camera or sensor row here?

device-test.formula:
Overall status = count of OK checks vs warnings.
OK = value present and within the healthy range.
Warning = value present but outside the healthy range (low battery, offline, cookies off).
Info = value unavailable or neutral (device guess, locale, touch-less desktop).
howTo: Leave the selector on Auto-detect, or pick your exact device from the list.
Read the checklist. Green means healthy, amber means worth a look, grey is neutral information.
Tap any warning and follow the hint - for example, charge the battery or enable cookies.
Press Copy report to share the full summary with a support team.
keyFacts: The checklist reads live values: browser, OS, screen, CPU cores, memory, touch, battery, network, and cookies.
Green (OK) means the value is present and healthy; amber (Warning) means check it; grey (Info) is neutral.
Battery level and charging state come from the Battery API, mainly available in Chrome and Edge.
The network row uses the Network Information API: connection type (like 4g) and downlink speed in Mb/s.
Touch points above zero means the device reports a touch screen - useful for confirming tablet mode.
The device guess combines the user agent with screen size; you can override it with the manual list.
device-test.keywords: device test, phone test online, check my device, device info, laptop test, tablet test, device health check
limitations: The battery and memory APIs are not supported in every browser - those rows may show Unknown.
The device guess is a heuristic, not a guarantee; always confirm with the manual list.
This summary cannot test hardware quality - use the dedicated keyboard, mic, camera, and sensor tests for that.
Values reflect this browser only; another browser on the same device may report differently.

device-test.quickAnswer: The Device Test reads your browser, operating system, screen size, CPU cores, memory, touch support, battery level, network type, and cookie setting through real browser APIs, then shows them as a colour-coded checklist. Pick your device from the list (Android phone, iPhone, iPad, MacBook, laptop, desktop, tablet, smartwatch) or leave auto-detect on. Copy the report to share it with support.
device-test.tagline: One checklist for your whole device - browser, OS, screen, CPU, battery, and network.
device-test.workedExample:
You run the test on your phone with Auto-detect:
1. Device row shows Auto-detect: Android phone - correct.
2. Browser row shows Chrome 126, OS row shows Android 14 - both green.
3. Battery row shows 15%, not charging - amber warning, so you plug in the charger.
4. Network row shows 4g, 10 Mb/s - green.
5. Cookies row shows disabled - amber warning. You enable them and the row turns green.
You press Copy report and send it to support.
